source.author: cic
source.text: est etiam quiete et pure atque eleganter actae aetatis placida ac lenis senectus, qualem accepimus Platonis, qui uno et octogesimo anno scribens est mortuus, qualem Isocratis, qui eum librum, qui Panathenaicus inscribitur, quarto nonagesimo anno scripsisse dicit vixitque quinquennium postea; cuius magister Leontinus Gorgias centum et septem complevit annos, neque umquam in suo studio atque opere cessavit.
source.text_original: est etiam quiete et pure atque eleganter actae aetatis placida ac lenis senectus, qualem accepimus Platonis, qui uno et octogesimo anno scribens est mortuus, qualem Isocratis, qui eum librum, qui Panathenaicus inscribitur, quarto nonagesimo anno scripsisse dicit vixitque quinquennium postea; cuius magister Leontinus Gorgias centum et septem complevit annos, neque umquam in suo studio atque opere cessavit.
source.text_english: There is also a calm and gentle old age of a life spent in tranquillity, purity, and refinement, such as we know Plato had, who died while writing in his eighty-first year, and such as Isocrates had, who says that he wrote the book entitled Panathenaicus in his ninety-fourth year and lived for five years afterward; his teacher, the Leontine Gorgias, completed one hundred and seven years and never once ceased from his study and work.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: unde et sapiens ille Graeciae, cum expletis centum et septem annis se mori cerneret, dixisse fertur dolere, quod tunc egrederetur e uita, quando sapere coepisset; Plato octogesimo et uno anno scribens est mortuus; Isocrates nonaginta et nouem annos in docendi scribendique labore compleuit; taceo ceteros philosophos, Pythagoram, Democritum, Xenocratem, Zenonem, Cleanthem, qui iam aetate longaeua in sapientiae studiis floruerunt: ad poetas uenio , Homerum, Hesiodum, Simonidem, Stesichorum, qui grandes natu cygneum nescio quid et solito dulcius uicina morte cecinerunt.
reuse.text_original: unde et sapiens ille Graeciae, cum expletis centum et septem annis se mori cerneret, dixisse fertur dolere, quod tunc egrederetur e uita, quando sapere coepisset; Plato octogesimo et uno anno scribens est mortuus; Isocrates nonaginta et nouem annos in docendi scribendique labore compleuit; taceo ceteros philosophos, Pythagoram, Democritum, Xenocratem, Zenonem, Cleanthem, qui iam aetate longaeua in sapientiae studiis floruerunt: ad poetas uenio , Homerum, Hesiodum, Simonidem, Stesichorum, qui grandes natu cygneum nescio quid et solito dulcius uicina morte cecinerunt.
reuse.text_english: Hence that wise man of Greece, when he saw that he had completed one hundred and seven years and was going to die, is said to have remarked with regret that he was then leaving life at the very time when he had begun to become wise; Plato died at the age of eighty-one, while still writing; Isocrates completed ninety-nine years in the labor of teaching and writing; I pass over the other philosophers, Pythagoras, Democritus, Xenocrates, Zeno, and Cleanthes, who in their very long old age flourished in the pursuit of wisdom: I come to the poets, Homer, Hesiod, Simonides, Stesichorus, who in advanced years, with death nearby, sang, I know not what, a swan-like song, sweeter than their wonted strain.
